title: Concrete Pathways & Footpaths: Brisbane Design Ideas (2026 Guide)
excerpt: Discover stunning concrete pathway and footpath design ideas for your Brisbane home. Explore finishes, edging, costs, and local council requirements for a durable and stylish walkway.
content:
Transform Your Brisbane Home with Stunning Concrete Pathways and Footpaths

A well-designed pathway does more than just connect two points; it guides the eye, enhances your landscape, and adds significant value and functionality to your property. For Brisbane homeowners, a durable and stylish concrete pathway is an essential investment that withstands our unique subtropical climate while boosting kerb appeal. Whether you're creating a welcoming entrance, a practical garden path, or a sleek walkway, the design possibilities with concrete are nearly endless.

At Concrete Concepts Group, we specialise in crafting high-quality concrete pathways in Brisbane that are as beautiful as they are long-lasting. Let's explore some design ideas to inspire your next project.

Why Concrete is the Smart Choice for Brisbane Walkways

Before diving into design, it's worth noting why concrete is the superior choice for pathways and footpaths in the Brisbane area. Its resilience against heavy rain, intense sun, and shifting soils makes it a low-maintenance and cost-effective solution. Unlike pavers that can shift or harbour weeds, a professionally laid concrete path provides a solid, continuous surface that remains stable for decades. From simple broom-finish footpaths to intricate decorative designs, concrete offers unmatched versatility.

Key Design Considerations for Your Concrete Pathway

Creating the perfect walkway concrete design in Brisbane involves several key decisions. Getting these elements right will ensure your path is not only visually appealing but also safe, functional, and compliant with local standards.

1. Pathway Width and Dimensions

The width of your pathway is crucial for both aesthetics and practicality. A primary entrance path should be wide enough for two people to walk side-by-side comfortably, typically 1.2 to 1.5 metres. For a secondary garden path with concrete, a width of 0.9 to 1.2 metres is often sufficient. It's also important to consider Brisbane City Council guidelines, which specify minimum widths for public-facing footpaths to ensure accessibility. As a fully licensed contractor (QBCC Licence #15299707), Concrete Concepts Group ensures all work complies with these local regulations.

2. Concrete Finishes: Finding Your Style

The finish of your concrete is where you can truly express your personal style. Here are some of the most popular options for Brisbane homes:

  • Exposed Aggregate: This is one of the most sought-after finishes for a concrete pathway in Brisbane. By washing away the top layer of cement paste, the natural stones and pebbles within the mix are revealed. The result is a textured, non-slip surface with a stunning, natural aesthetic. Learn more about our exposed aggregate services.
  • Coloured Concrete: Full-depth coloured concrete provides a consistent, vibrant hue that won't fade or chip over time. With a wide range of earthy tones and contemporary shades available, you can easily match your pathway to your home's exterior colour scheme.
  • Stencilled and Stamped Concrete: For a more decorative look, stencilling or stamping can replicate the appearance of bricks, pavers, or natural stone at a fraction of the cost. These are fantastic footpath concrete ideas for creating a high-end, custom look.
  • Broom Finish: The classic broom finish is a simple, cost-effective, and highly practical option. The fine-lined texture provides excellent slip resistance, making it a safe choice for any walkway.

3. Edging Options for a Polished Look

Edging adds a clean, defined border to your pathway, preventing grass from encroaching and creating a professional finish. Options range from an integrated concrete edge, formed as part of the main pour, to contrasting materials like brick, stone, or timber-look concrete sleepers. A well-defined edge can elevate a simple path into a deliberate design feature and is a key component of a quality concrete driveway as well.

4. Ensuring Proper Drainage

In a city known for its summer storms, drainage is a non-negotiable aspect of pathway design. A correctly installed concrete path should have a slight cross-fall (slope) to direct water away from your home's foundation and prevent pooling. In some cases, integrating channel drains or connecting the pathway's drainage to your property's existing stormwater system may be necessary. This is particularly important when the path is adjacent to retaining walls or other structures.

5. Integrating Pathway Lighting

Don't overlook the impact of lighting. Integrating low-voltage LED lighting along the edges of your concrete pathway not only enhances safety and security at night but also creates a beautiful ambient effect. Lights can be installed flush with the surface or on small posts alongside the path, highlighting its shape and texture after dark.

Estimated Costs for Concrete Pathways in Brisbane

The cost of a new concrete pathway depends on several factors, including the size, complexity of the design, site access, and the chosen finish. The table below provides a general guide to pricing in Brisbane. For a detailed and accurate quote tailored to your project, we recommend using our online calculator or contacting us directly.

Concrete Finish Estimated Price per Square Metre (m²) Best For
Standard Grey / Broom Finish $85 - $110 Utility paths, shed slabs, budget-conscious projects
Coloured Concrete $95 - $125 Matching home colour schemes, modern designs
Exposed Aggregate $120 - $160 Driveways, patios, pool surrounds, non-slip surfaces
Stencilled or Stamped Concrete $130 - $180+ Feature pathways, mimicking pavers or stone
Disclaimer: Prices are indicative only and can vary based on site conditions, preparation work required (such as excavation), and project complexity.

Why Choose Concrete Concepts Group?

When it comes to creating the perfect concrete pathway for your Brisbane home, you need a team with local experience and a commitment to quality. Concrete Concepts Group is a trusted, family-operated business that has been serving the Brisbane community for years. We understand the local climate and soil conditions, ensuring every concrete slab and pathway we pour is built to last. Our attention to detail and dedication to customer satisfaction are why homeowners across all the areas we service choose us for their concreting needs. Check out our customer reviews to see for yourself!

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does a new concrete pathway take to install?

A typical residential pathway project takes 2-4 days, including preparation, pouring, and initial curing. However, the concrete will need about 7 days before it can handle regular foot traffic and 28 days to reach its full strength.

Is a concrete pathway slippery when wet?

Not if the correct finish is applied. Finishes like exposed aggregate and broom finish are specifically designed to provide excellent texture and slip resistance, making them very safe even in wet conditions.

Do I need council approval for a new footpath?

For pathways entirely on your private property, you generally don't need council approval. However, if the work involves the crossover (the part of the driveway on council land) or affects the public footpath, a permit from Brisbane City Council is required. We can help manage this process for you.

Can you remove my old, cracked pathway?

Absolutely. Concrete Concepts Group provides a complete service, which includes the demolition and removal of old concrete, site preparation, and the installation of your new pathway.

How do I maintain my new concrete path?

Concrete paths are very low maintenance. We recommend a simple clean with a pressure washer every 12-18 months. For decorative surfaces like exposed aggregate or coloured concrete, re-sealing every 2-3 years will protect the surface and keep it looking vibrant.

What's the difference between a path and a patio?

While both are paved surfaces, a pathway is primarily for transit, connecting different areas. A concrete patio is a larger, destination space designed for outdoor living and recreation. We specialise in both!

title: Is Concrete Resurfacing Worth It in Brisbane? When to Overlay vs. Replace (2026)
excerpt: Torn between resurfacing or replacing your concrete in Brisbane? Our guide breaks down the costs, benefits, and when to choose a concrete overlay versus a full replacement for your driveway or patio.
content:
Is Concrete Resurfacing Worth It in Brisbane? When to Overlay vs. Replace

Your concrete driveway, patio, or pool surround has served you well for years, but now it’s looking a little worse for wear. Perhaps it's covered in stains, riddled with fine cracks, or the colour has faded under the harsh Brisbane sun. You’re faced with a common dilemma for Queensland homeowners: should you opt for a concrete overlay, or is it time for a full replacement? Making the right choice is crucial for both your budget and your property's long-term value.

This guide will explore the critical differences between concrete resurfacing and replacement, helping you decide which is the smarter investment for your home. We'll compare costs, durability, and the ideal situations for each, giving you the confidence to make an informed decision. As Brisbane's trusted concreting specialists, Concrete Concepts Group is here to provide clarity on this important topic.

Concrete Resurfacing vs. Full Replacement: A Head-to-Head Comparison

Understanding the fundamental differences between a resurfacing overlay (often called covercrete) and a complete tear-out-and-replace job is the first step. One is a cosmetic facelift, while the other is major surgery. Let's break down how they stack up against each other.

Feature Concrete Resurfacing (Overlay) Full Concrete Replacement
Cost Lower upfront cost ($50 - $100 per m²) Higher upfront cost ($100 - $150+ per m²)
Lifespan/Durability 5-10 years, dependent on base integrity 20-30+ years, a brand new installation
Ideal For Surface-level issues: stains, hairline cracks, fading, updating aesthetics. Structural problems: deep cracks, sinking, crumbling, poor foundation.
Turnaround Time Fast (2-4 days) Longer (1-2 weeks), includes demolition and curing
Appearance/Customisation Excellent. Wide range of colours, patterns, and finishes available. Excellent. A blank slate for any finish, including exposed aggregate or coloured concrete.

The Big Question: What Are the Costs in Brisbane?

For most homeowners, the budget is the deciding factor. It’s important to understand not just the price per square metre, but what that price includes. Here’s a detailed look at what you can expect to pay in the Brisbane market.

Concrete Resurfacing (Covercrete/Overlay) Costs in Brisbane

A concrete overlay is a highly cost-effective way to rejuvenate your concrete. The price for professional concrete resurfacing in Brisbane typically ranges from $50 to $100 per square metre. This variation depends on several factors:

  • Surface Condition: The more preparation required (grinding, extensive crack repair), the higher the cost.
  • Complexity of Finish: A simple, single-colour overlay will be cheaper than an intricate, multi-coloured stencil pattern designed to mimic tiles or pavers.
  • Job Size: Larger areas often have a slightly lower per-metre rate than smaller, more intricate jobs.

Sample Concrete Resurfacing Costs (Brisbane)

Finish Type Estimated Price per Square Metre Best For
Standard Spray-On (Plain Colour) $50 - $75 Refreshing driveways, patios, and pathways with a clean, uniform look.
Stencil Pattern Overlay $70 - $100 Creating a decorative, high-end look like brick, tile, or cobblestone.
Fleck / Multi-Colour Finish $65 - $90 Hiding imperfections and adding visual texture to pool surrounds or patios.

Full Concrete Replacement Costs in Brisbane

When your concrete is beyond a simple facelift, a full replacement is the only long-term solution. The cost for a new concrete driveway or slab in Brisbane generally falls between $100 and $150 per square metre, but can go higher for complex projects. This price typically includes:

  • Demolition and Removal: Breaking up and hauling away the old, failed concrete.
  • Excavation and Base Preparation: Ensuring a stable foundation for the new slab, which may involve work from our excavation team.
  • Formwork and Reinforcement: Setting up the perimeter and laying steel mesh for strength.
  • The Concrete Pour: The supply and professional installation of the new concrete.
  • Finishing: The final surface treatment, whether it's a simple broom finish or a decorative style.

Factors like tight site access, the need for a concrete pump, or significant earthworks for retaining walls can increase the overall project cost. You can get a more precise estimate using our online concrete calculator.

When to Resurface: The Smart Choice for a Fresh Look

Opting for a concrete overlay is an excellent decision when the underlying slab is structurally sound. If your concrete's problems are only skin-deep, resurfacing is your best friend. Choose to resurface when you see:

  • Superficial Blemishes: Stains from oil, leaves, or rust that cleaning can't remove.
  • Hairline Cracks: Minor, non-structural cracks that are less than 2mm wide.
  • Faded Colour: The original colour has been bleached out by the sun and elements.
  • You Want a New Look: You’re simply tired of the plain grey and want to upgrade your home's curb appeal with a modern colour or pattern.

The primary benefits are clear: it’s significantly cheaper, the transformation is incredibly fast, and the design possibilities are vast. A resurfacing job by Concrete Concepts Group can give your property a premium look in just a few days.

When to Replace: Addressing Deeper Issues

A pretty overlay can't fix a broken foundation. Applying a new surface over deeply flawed concrete is like putting a band-aid on a broken arm—it hides the problem but doesn't solve it. Full replacement is non-negotiable when you have:

  • Deep, Structural Cracks: Large, wide cracks (wider than a credit card) that go through the slab.
  • Sinking or Heaving: Sections of the concrete are noticeably lower or higher than others, indicating major ground movement or a failed sub-base.
  • Spalling or Crumbling: The surface is flaking away, and the concrete is breaking apart. This can be a sign of "concrete cancer" where the internal steel reinforcement is rusting.
  • Widespread Damage: If more than 30-40% of the surface is covered in deep cracks or other serious issues, replacement is often more economical in the long run.

While the upfront cost is higher, a new concrete slab is a long-term investment in your property's safety and stability. It gives you peace of mind knowing the foundation is solid for decades to come.

The Concrete Resurfacing Process: A Step-by-Step Guide

A professional resurfacing job is a multi-stage process that requires precision and expertise. Here’s how we do it:

  1. Inspection and Assessment: We first evaluate the existing slab to confirm it's a suitable candidate for resurfacing.
  2. Surface Preparation: This is the most critical step. The surface is thoroughly cleaned with a high-pressure washer to remove dirt and debris. We then use a diamond grinder to open the pores of the concrete and create a rough profile for the new layer to grip onto.
  3. Crack Repair: Any minor cracks are filled with a flexible epoxy or polymer compound.
  4. Primer/Base Coat: A polymer-modified cementitious primer is applied to ensure a powerful chemical bond between the old and new surfaces.
  5. Application of Overlay: We spray the chosen cement-based overlay in two or more coats to achieve the desired texture and thickness. If a pattern is desired, a stencil is laid down before this stage.
  6. Sealing: Two coats of a high-quality, UV-stable acrylic sealer are applied. This is vital in Brisbane's climate to protect against moisture, stains, and fading, and can include an anti-slip additive for safety around pools and on steep driveways.

Brisbane-Specific Considerations

Brisbane’s unique environment plays a role in your decision. Our subtropical climate, with its high humidity and intense summer storms, means moisture is a constant enemy. For both resurfacing and new slabs, effective sealing is non-negotiable to prevent mould growth and water penetration. Furthermore, some of Brisbane's reactive clay soils can cause ground movement, making a strong, well-prepared sub-base for new slabs across the region absolutely critical.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does concrete resurfacing last?

A professionally installed concrete overlay can last between 8 to 15 years, depending on the quality of the installation, the condition of the underlying slab, and how well it is maintained. Regular cleaning and resealing every 2-3 years is key to its longevity.

Can you resurface a painted or sealed driveway?

Yes, but the existing coating must be completely removed first. This is usually done by diamond grinding to get back to the bare concrete. Applying an overlay on top of paint or a failing sealer will cause it to peel off.

Is resurfaced concrete slippery?

It doesn’t have to be. During the sealing process, a special anti-slip additive can be mixed into the sealer. This is highly recommended for pool surrounds, steep driveways, and commercial areas to ensure safety, especially in wet conditions.

How soon can I walk or drive on my newly resurfaced concrete?

You can typically walk on the surface after 24 hours. However, you should wait at least 7 days before driving a vehicle on it to allow the sealer to fully cure and harden.

What’s the difference between covercrete and a concrete overlay?

They are essentially the same thing. "Covercrete" is a brand name that has become a common term for the process of applying a spray-on cementitious topping or overlay to existing concrete.

Do I need a council permit for concrete resurfacing in Brisbane?

Generally, no. Since you are not changing the footprint or structure of the slab, Brisbane City Council permits are not typically required for resurfacing. However, a full replacement of a large driveway may require approval.

Why should I hire a licensed contractor like Concrete Concepts Group?

Hiring a fully licensed and insured contractor is your best protection. Concrete Concepts Group holds a current QBCC Licence (#15299707), which guarantees our work meets Australian Standards and that you are protected. Unlicensed operators offer no such security. Check out our customer reviews to see why Brisbane trusts us.

Your Brisbane Concreting Experts

Ultimately, whether concrete resurfacing is worth it depends entirely on the condition of your existing slab. If it's structurally sound, a concrete overlay is a fantastic and affordable way to transform your property. If there are deeper issues at play, a full replacement is the only responsible long-term solution. For an honest, expert assessment and a flawless finish, look no further than the team at Concrete Concepts Group. Explore our blog for more tips and insights.

title: How to Fix Cracked Concrete: DIY vs Professional Repair (2026 Guide)
excerpt: Frustrated by cracked concrete? Our Brisbane guide covers DIY fixes vs. professional repairs, helping you identify crack types, understand costs, and decide when to call an expert.
content:
How to Fix Cracked Concrete: A Brisbane Homeowner's Guide

Discovering a crack in your concrete driveway, patio, or slab can be disheartening. In a city like Brisbane, with its unique subtropical climate, concrete is put to the test. From scorching summer heat to sudden downpours, the weather can play a significant role in the appearance of cracks. But don't despair! Many cracks are purely cosmetic and can be easily addressed. The real question is whether it's a simple DIY fix or a job for a professional. This guide will walk you through everything you need to know about concrete crack repair in Brisbane, helping you decide on the best course of action.

Understanding the Different Types of Concrete Cracks

Not all cracks are created equal. Identifying the type of crack you're dealing with is the first step towards a successful repair. Here are the most common types you'll encounter in Brisbane homes:

1. Hairline Cracks

As the name suggests, these are very fine, shallow cracks on the surface of the concrete. They are often caused by plastic shrinkage during the curing process, especially in Brisbane's hot and humid climate where the surface can dry too quickly. While unsightly, hairline cracks are generally not a structural concern. A simple DIY repair is often sufficient.

2. Structural Cracks

These are more serious and indicate a problem with the concrete's structural integrity. They are typically wider than a credit card, run through the entire depth of the slab, and may show signs of vertical displacement. Structural cracks can be caused by poor soil compaction, overloading the slab, or significant ground movement. If you suspect a structural crack, it's crucial to call a professional for an assessment. Ignoring them can lead to further damage and costly repairs down the line.

3. Settlement Cracks

Settlement cracks occur when the ground beneath the concrete slab shifts or settles, causing the concrete to crack under the strain. These cracks are common in Brisbane due to the reactive clay soils found in many suburbs. You might notice them after a period of heavy rain or prolonged drought. Settlement cracks can vary in severity, from minor to significant. A professional should assess the situation to determine the cause and recommend the best course of action, which might involve underpinning or other foundation repair methods.

DIY Concrete Crack Repair: What You Can Tackle Yourself

For minor hairline cracks and small chips, a DIY approach can be a cost-effective solution. If you're a handy homeowner, here's how you can tackle these repairs:

Tools and Materials:

  • Wire brush
  • Broom or leaf blower
  • Caulking gun
  • Concrete crack filler or sealant
  • Trowel or putty knife

Step-by-Step Guide:

  1. Clean the crack: Use a wire brush to remove any loose debris, dirt, or old sealant from the crack. A broom or leaf blower can help to clear away the dust.
  2. Apply the filler: Load the concrete crack filler into the caulking gun and apply it into the crack. Make sure to fill the entire depth of the crack.
  3. Smooth the surface: Use a trowel or putty knife to smooth the filler, ensuring it is level with the surrounding concrete.
  4. Allow to cure: Follow the manufacturer's instructions for curing times. This is especially important in Brisbane's climate, as humidity can affect drying times.

For a seamless finish, you can find coloured sealants to match your existing concrete. Remember, this DIY method is only suitable for non-structural cracks. For anything more significant, it's time to call in the experts.

When to Call a Professional for Concrete Crack Repair in Brisbane

While DIY repairs are great for minor issues, some situations demand the expertise of a licensed professional. Attempting to fix major concrete problems yourself can often lead to more significant damage and higher costs in the long run. Here’s when you should pick up the phone and call a specialist like Concrete Concepts Group:

  • Wide or Deep Cracks: If a crack is wider than a credit card (about 5mm) or you can't see the bottom of it, it's a sign of a potentially serious issue.
  • Uneven Surfaces (Tripping Hazards): When one side of the crack is higher than the other, this indicates ground movement or settlement. This is a significant structural problem and a serious safety hazard that requires professional assessment.
  • Water Pooling in Cracks: Water actively seeping into or pooling in cracks can accelerate deterioration, especially in Brisbane's humid climate which can promote mould growth and concrete cancer (spalling).
  • Spiderweb or Alligator Cracking: A network of interconnected cracks across a large area often points to a failing sub-base or widespread surface failure.
  • Structural Concerns: If the cracked concrete is part of a load-bearing structure like a foundation, retaining wall, or suspended slab, you must consult a professional. Concrete Concepts Group is fully licensed (QBCC Licence #15299707) to handle these critical structural repairs.

A professional concreter will not only fix the visible crack but also diagnose and address the underlying cause, ensuring a long-lasting and safe solution. They have the right equipment, materials, and experience to handle complex repairs, from epoxy injections for structural cracks to slab jacking for settled concrete.

Concrete Repair Costs in Brisbane

The cost of repairing cracked concrete in Brisbane can vary significantly based on the type and extent of the damage. Below is a general guide to what you can expect to pay. For an accurate, obligation-free quote tailored to your specific needs, it’s always best to contact a professional.

Repair Type Estimated Cost (per metre or job) Best For
DIY Crack Filler Kit $30 - $80 per kit Minor hairline cracks (less than 5mm wide) on non-structural surfaces like patios or paths.
Professional Crack Injection (Epoxy/Polyurethane) $70 - $150 per linear metre Structural cracks in foundations, slabs, and walls to restore strength and prevent water ingress.
Concrete Resurfacing $50 - $90 per square metre Widespread surface crazing, discolouration, or minor imperfections on driveways or patios.
Slab Jacking / Underpinning $500 - $3,000+ per job Sunken or settled slabs caused by soil movement, often a more complex and costly repair.

*Please note: These prices are indicative only and can be influenced by factors such as site access, job complexity, and the specific materials required.

Repair vs. Replacement: Which is the Right Choice?

In some cases, repairing the concrete may not be the most cost-effective or long-term solution. If the damage is extensive, or if the underlying cause is severe, replacement might be the better option. Here’s a quick comparison to help you decide:

"Deciding whether to repair or replace your concrete depends on the extent and type of damage. In many cases, repairs can be a cost-effective way to extend the life of your concrete, but for severe deterioration, replacement is often the smarter investment." - Concrete Concepts Group

When to Repair:

  • The cracks are mostly cosmetic and not structural.
  • The slab is otherwise in good condition and structurally sound.
  • The cost of repair is significantly less than 25-40% of the replacement cost.
  • You're looking for a quick and budget-friendly solution. Check out our cost calculator for a preliminary estimate.

When to Replace:

  • The concrete has numerous, deep, and interconnected cracks (alligator cracking).
  • The slab is severely settled, heaved, or has significant height differences.
  • The concrete is crumbling, spalling, or showing signs of advanced deterioration (concrete cancer).
  • The sub-base has failed, requiring a complete re-do. Explore our slab services for more information.

For a professional opinion on your specific situation, the team at Concrete Concepts Group can provide a thorough assessment and honest advice. We service all areas across Brisbane.

Frequently Asked Questions

How does Brisbane’s climate affect concrete cracking?

Brisbane's subtropical climate, with its high humidity, intense summer heat, and heavy rainfall, creates a challenging environment for concrete. The rapid temperature fluctuations can cause concrete to expand and contract, leading to stress cracks. Furthermore, the heavy clay soils in many parts of Brisbane swell when wet and shrink when dry, causing ground movement that can lead to significant settlement cracks in driveways and patios.

Do I need a permit from Brisbane City Council to repair my driveway?

For minor crack repairs, you typically do not need a permit. However, if the repair involves altering the driveway's dimensions, location, or requires substantial reconstruction, you will likely need to apply for a residential driveway permit from Brisbane City Council. It's always best to check their official website or consult with a professional who is familiar with local regulations.

Can a cracked concrete slab be saved?

Absolutely! In many cases, a cracked slab can be successfully repaired, especially if the damage is addressed early. Techniques like epoxy injection can restore the structural integrity of a slab, while resurfacing can fix cosmetic issues. The key is a proper assessment by a professional to determine the cause and extent of the cracking. See what our customers are saying on our reviews page.

What is concrete cancer and can it be repaired?

Concrete cancer, or spalling, occurs when the steel reinforcement within a concrete slab begins to rust. The rust expands, displacing the surrounding concrete and causing it to crack and break away. It is often caused by water penetration through unprotected cracks. Yes, it can be repaired, but it's a complex process that involves removing the damaged concrete, treating the rusted steel, and then patching the area. This is a job strictly for professionals, like the team at Concrete Concepts Group.

Is it cheaper to repair or replace a cracked driveway?

Repairing is almost always cheaper in the short term. However, the decision should be based on the long-term value. If your driveway has minor cracks and is structurally sound, a repair or resurfacing is a cost-effective choice. If it has deep, widespread cracks, significant settlement, or a failed sub-base, replacing it might be a better investment to avoid recurring problems. Our blog has more articles to help you make an informed decision.

Your Trusted Partner for Concrete Repairs in Brisbane

Don't let cracked concrete compromise the safety and appearance of your property. Whether it's a minor fix or a major structural repair, tackling the problem correctly is key to a lasting solution. For professional advice and expert service you can trust, look no further than Concrete Concepts Group. Our experienced, QBCC-licensed team has the skills to diagnose the root cause of the problem and deliver the highest quality repairs.

title: How to Choose the Right Concreter in Brisbane: 10 Questions to Ask
excerpt: Hiring the right concreter in Brisbane is crucial. This guide provides 10 essential questions to ask any potential contractor to ensure you hire a true professional for your project.
content:
How to Choose the Right Concreter in Brisbane: 10 Questions to Ask

Choosing the right concreter for your project in Brisbane is a critical decision. The quality of their workmanship will determine the longevity, safety, and appearance of your concrete structure for years to come. Whether you're planning a new concrete driveway, a stylish exposed aggregate patio, or a sturdy retaining wall, asking the right questions upfront can save you from costly mistakes and headaches down the track. This guide will walk you through the ten essential questions you must ask any potential concreter to ensure you're hiring a true professional.

Brisbane's unique subtropical climate, with its high humidity, intense summer storms, and reactive clay soils, presents specific challenges for concrete work. A reputable local concreter will understand these conditions and use the appropriate techniques and materials to ensure a durable, long-lasting finish. At Concrete Concepts Group, we've been navigating these local challenges for years, delivering exceptional results for our clients across the city.

1. Are You a QBCC Licensed Concreter?

This is the most important question you can ask. In Queensland, any concreting work valued over $3,300 (including labour and materials) legally requires a licence from the Queensland Building and Construction Commission (QBCC). A valid licence demonstrates that the concreter has met the required qualifications, has the necessary technical skills, and is financially sound.

You can easily check a concreter's licence status on the QBCC website. Our QBCC licence number is 15299707, and we encourage all potential clients to verify it. Hiring an unlicensed operator not only puts you at risk of substandard work but also means you won't have access to the QBCC's dispute resolution services or home warranty insurance if something goes wrong. Don't just take their word for it—always check the licence yourself.

2. Do You Have Current Public Liability Insurance?

Accidents can happen on any construction site. Public liability insurance protects you, the homeowner, from financial liability if there is an accident that causes injury to a person or damage to your property (or a neighbour's property). Ask to see a copy of their Certificate of Currency. A professional concreter will have no hesitation in providing this. A typical policy for a residential concreter should cover at least $10 million. This insurance is your safety net, ensuring you're not left with a hefty bill for unforeseen incidents.

3. Can You Provide References and Examples of Your Work?

A picture is worth a thousand words, and in concreting, seeing is believing. Ask for a portfolio of their completed projects, especially those similar to what you have in mind. Better yet, ask for addresses of recent jobs in your area so you can drive by and see the quality of their finish firsthand. Reputable concreters will also be able to provide you with contact details for recent clients who have agreed to act as referees. Take the time to call them and ask about their experience. Check out our reviews page to see what our happy clients have to say about Concrete Concepts Group.

4. What Warranty or Guarantee Do You Offer on Your Work?

A professional concreter will stand by their work. Ask about the warranty they provide on both their workmanship and the materials used. This should be clearly stated in your written contract. While concrete itself can be prone to minor hairline cracking (which is normal), a warranty should cover significant structural failures or defects resulting from poor workmanship, such as major cracking, spalling, or an uneven finish. Understanding the terms of the warranty will give you peace of mind.

5. What Concrete Strength (MPa) Will You Use?

Not all concrete is created equal. The strength of concrete is measured in megapascals (MPa). The required strength depends on the application. For a standard driveway that will support passenger vehicles, 25 MPa is the recommended minimum. For a patio or pathway, 20 MPa might suffice. For a heavy-duty concrete slab intended for a shed or to support heavy vehicles, 32 MPa or even 40 MPa may be necessary. An experienced concreter will recommend the correct strength for your specific project, ensuring it complies with Australian Standards.

6. What Reinforcement Will Be Used?

Concrete has excellent compressive strength but is weak in tension. Steel reinforcement (reo) is used to give it the necessary tensile strength, helping to control cracking and hold the slab together. The type and placement of this reinforcement are critical. For most residential projects in Brisbane, this will involve steel mesh (e.g., SL72 or SL82) placed on "chairs" to ensure it sits in the middle of the concrete's thickness, not on the ground. The concreter should be able to explain the reinforcement plan for your project and why it's appropriate.

7. How Will You Manage Site Preparation and Drainage?

A great concrete job starts with a solid foundation. Proper site preparation is non-negotiable. This involves excavation to the correct depth, establishing a stable sub-base of compacted road base or crusher dust, and setting up formwork to define the shape of the pour. Crucially, the concreter must account for drainage. In a city like Brisbane, with its sudden downpours, ensuring water flows away from your house and foundation is paramount. The surface should be sloped correctly (a fall of at least 1:100 or 10mm per metre is standard) towards a drain, garden bed, or street. Poor drainage can lead to water pooling, erosion, and costly structural damage to your home.

8. What is the Estimated Timeline for the Project?

A professional concreter should be able to provide a clear timeline for your project, from site preparation to the final clean-up. This should include key milestones such as the excavation, formwork setup, the day of the concrete pour, and the curing time required before you can walk or drive on the surface. While weather can sometimes cause unavoidable delays, especially in Brisbane, a clear schedule helps manage expectations and allows you to plan accordingly. Be wary of a concreter who is vague about the timeline.

9. What Are Your Payment Terms?

Understand the payment schedule before you sign any contract. It is standard practice to pay a deposit, but this should not be an excessive amount. Under QBCC regulations, for contracts between $3,300 and $20,000, the maximum deposit is 10%. For contracts over $20,000, it's 5%. The contract should then outline a series of progress payments at the completion of specific stages. The final payment should only be due after the job is 100% complete and you are satisfied with the work. Never pay the full amount upfront. At Concrete Concepts Group, we provide a clear, itemised quote and a fair payment schedule in line with all regulations.

10. Does Your Quote Include Site Cleanup?

This might seem like a minor detail, but it makes a big difference. A concreting project can generate a significant amount of mess, including excavated soil, old concrete, timber off-cuts from formwork, and concrete slurry. A professional operator will factor site cleanup into their quote. This means they will leave your property tidy, removing all construction debris and washing down adjacent surfaces. Clarify this from the outset to avoid any nasty surprises or being left with a pile of rubbish to deal with yourself.

Comparing Concreter Quotes: A Quick Guide

When you receive quotes, it's not just about the final price. Use a table to compare what each concreter is offering. This helps you see the true value and ensure you're comparing apples with apples.

Feature Concreter A Concreter B Concrete Concepts Group
QBCC Licence Check Yes No Yes (15299707)
Concrete Strength (MPa) 20 MPa Not Specified 25 MPa (min. for driveways)
Reinforcement Mesh Mesh (unspecified) SL72/SL82 on chairs
Drainage Plan Vague Yes Detailed Fall & Drains
Warranty 12 Months None Comprehensive Workmanship Warranty
Includes Cleanup No Yes Yes, Full Site Cleanup

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does concrete take to cure in Brisbane?

While you can typically walk on new concrete after 24-48 hours, it takes about 7 days before you can drive a passenger car on it. However, concrete doesn't reach its full specified strength for 28 days. The humid Brisbane climate can sometimes affect drying times, but your concreter will provide specific advice.

Do I need council approval for my concreting project?

For most standard driveways, patios, and pathways on residential lots, you won't need council approval from Brisbane City Council. However, if you are building a new crossover (the part of the driveway on the council verge), building a retaining wall over 1 metre high, or if your property is subject to character or heritage overlays, you will likely need approval. Always check the council requirements for your specific area.

What is the difference between exposed aggregate and plain concrete?

Plain concrete has a smooth, grey finish. Exposed aggregate is a decorative finish where the top layer of cement paste is washed away to reveal the small stones (aggregate) underneath. It provides a beautiful, textured, and non-slip surface, making it a very popular choice for Brisbane homes.

How much does concreting cost in Brisbane?

The cost of concreting varies significantly based on the type of finish, complexity of the job, site access, and required preparation. As a rough guide, you can expect to pay between $75 to $150 per square metre. For a more accurate and detailed quote, use our online concrete calculator.

Why is my new concrete cracking?

Minor hairline cracks are a normal part of the concrete curing process and are generally not a structural concern. These are called shrinkage cracks. However, large, deep, or growing cracks can indicate a problem with the sub-base, the concrete mix, or the reinforcement. This is why hiring a reputable concreter who guarantees their work is so important.

Choosing the right concreter is the most important step towards a successful project. By asking these ten questions, you can confidently vet potential contractors and find a skilled, licensed, and insured professional. For a no-obligation quote from a team that ticks all the boxes, Call 0424 463 268 or get a free quote at concreteconcepts.org.

title: Stencilled vs. Stamped Concrete: Which is Best for Brisbane?
excerpt: Considering decorative concrete? This guide compares stencilled and stamped concrete in Brisbane, covering costs, durability, patterns, and pros and cons to help you choose the best finish for your home.
content:
Stencilled Concrete vs. Stamped Concrete: A Brisbane Homeowner’s Guide

When it comes to enhancing your Brisbane home’s kerb appeal, a decorative concrete finish for your driveway, patio, or pathway is an exceptional choice. It offers the perfect blend of durability and design flexibility. Two of the most popular decorative concrete techniques are stencilling and stamping. While both create beautiful, textured surfaces, they involve different processes and offer distinct advantages. If you're weighing up stencilled concrete Brisbane versus stamped concrete Brisbane, this guide will walk you through the key differences to help you make an informed decision for your property.

What is Stencilled Concrete?

Stencilled concrete is a fantastic way to add pattern and colour to a concrete surface. The process involves laying down a large, disposable paper stencil over freshly laid concrete. A dry-shake colour hardener is then broadcast over the surface and trowelled in. Once the concrete has cured sufficiently, the stencil is removed, revealing a decorative pattern with realistic-looking ‘grout’ lines. The surface is then cleaned and sealed to protect it from the elements and wear. This technique is perfect for creating the look of bricks, pavers, or tiles without the higher cost and maintenance. It results in a relatively flat, textured surface, making it a practical and safe option for driveways and patios.

What is Stamped Concrete?

Stamped concrete, on the other hand, offers a more three-dimensional and realistic texture. The process involves pressing large, flexible polyurethane stamps into the surface of the concrete while it's still plastic. These stamps are moulded from real materials like slate, stone, brick, and even timber, allowing them to impart a highly authentic and detailed texture. Colour is often added through a combination of colour hardeners and release agents, which create depth and variation. The result is a stunning, high-end finish that can perfectly mimic expensive paving materials. Its robust and textured nature makes it a popular choice for pool surrounds, outdoor entertaining areas, and feature driveways.

Detailed Comparison: Stencil vs. Stamp Concrete in Brisbane

Choosing between stencilled and stamped concrete depends on your budget, aesthetic preferences, and the specific application. Here’s a direct comparison of the two techniques.

Process and Appearance

The most significant difference lies in the final look and feel. Stencilled concrete creates a pattern on the surface, resulting in a flatter finish with defined, coloured grout lines. It’s an excellent mimic of pavers or tiles from a distance. Stamped concrete creates a deeper, three-dimensional impression that replicates the authentic texture of the material it’s mimicking. The texture is not just visual; it’s physical, providing a more realistic and often more dramatic effect.

Cost Comparison for Brisbane Properties

For many homeowners, the budget is a deciding factor. While prices can vary based on project size, complexity, and site preparation needs, here is a general guide to costs in the Brisbane area.

Concrete Finish Estimated Cost per Square Metre (inc. GST) Key Considerations
Stencilled Concrete $90 - $125 A more budget-friendly decorative option. Price depends on pattern complexity and number of colours.
Stamped Concrete $120 - $170+ Higher cost due to more intensive labour and specialised equipment (stamps). Intricate patterns and custom colours increase the price.

Note: These prices are estimates. For an accurate, fixed-price quote, it’s always best to consult with a professional concreting contractor like Concrete Concepts Group.

Durability and Maintenance in Brisbane's Climate

Both stencilled and stamped concrete are incredibly durable and, when properly installed and sealed, will last for decades. In Brisbane’s subtropical climate, with its harsh sun and heavy seasonal rain, sealing is non-negotiable. A high-quality, UV-stable sealer protects the colour from fading and prevents water ingress, which can lead to cracking and surface degradation. We recommend resealing every 2-3 years to keep your decorative concrete looking its best. For cleaning, a simple wash with a pressure cleaner on a low setting is usually all that’s required. Stamped concrete’s deeper grooves may require a little more effort to clean than the flatter surface of stencilled concrete.

Best Applications

  • Stencilled Concrete: Its flatter profile makes it an excellent, low-slip choice for driveways, pathways, and general-use patios. The defined patterns are great for adding a formal, neat appearance to your home's exterior.
  • Stamped Concrete: The superior texture and aesthetic appeal make it ideal for feature areas like pool surrounds (with a non-slip additive in the sealer), alfresco dining spaces, and grand entranceways. It’s the go-to for achieving a luxurious, natural stone or timber look.

Popular Decorative Concrete Patterns in Brisbane

Both techniques offer a wide array of patterns. Some popular choices among Brisbane homeowners include:

  • For Stencilling: Cobblestone, Basketweave Brick, Ashlar Slate, and various tile patterns.
  • For Stamping: European Fan, Random Stone, Ashlar Cut Slate, and timber plank patterns.

Pros and Cons: A Quick Summary

Stencilled Concrete

Pros:

  • More affordable than stamped concrete.
  • Wide variety of patterns and colours available.
  • The flatter surface is generally less slippery.
  • The process is typically faster than stamping.

Cons:

  • The texture is not as realistic or three-dimensional as stamped concrete.
  • The surface pattern can show wear over many years in high-traffic areas if not properly maintained.

Stamped Concrete

Pros:

  • Creates a highly realistic, premium 3D texture.
  • Extremely durable and long-lasting.
  • Significantly adds to your property’s aesthetic and resale value.
  • Vast range of patterns that mimic natural materials.

Cons:

  • Higher initial installation cost.
  • Can be slippery when wet unless a non-slip additive is incorporated into the final sealing coat.
  • Repairs can be more complex to colour and pattern match perfectly.

Making the Right Choice for Your Brisbane Home

Ultimately, the best choice between stencil vs stamp concrete comes down to your personal style, your budget, and how you plan to use the space. If you desire a highly realistic, textured finish and see the project as a long-term investment in your home’s value, stamped concrete is an unparalleled choice. If you are looking for a cost-effective way to achieve a beautiful, patterned look that is both durable and practical, stencilled concrete is an excellent alternative. At Concrete Concepts Group, we specialise in all forms of decorative concrete. As a fully licensed and insured company (QBCC Licence #15299707), our experienced team can provide expert advice to help you select the perfect finish for your project. We can also discuss other popular options like exposed aggregate for a different, modern look.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is stamped or stencilled concrete slippery?

Any sealed concrete surface can be slippery when wet. However, this is easily managed. For stamped concrete, especially around pools, we always incorporate a non-slip polymer grit into the sealing coat, which creates a safe, textured surface. Stencilled concrete is naturally less slippery due to its flatter profile.

How long does decorative concrete last?

With proper installation and maintenance, both stencilled and stamped concrete surfaces can last for 25 years or more. The key is regular cleaning and resealing every 2-3 years to protect it from Brisbane’s climate.

Can you repair stamped and stencilled concrete?

Yes, repairs are possible. Stencilled concrete is generally easier to repair or resurface. Stamped concrete repairs can be more challenging to blend seamlessly with the existing pattern and colour, which is why it’s crucial to use an experienced contractor like Concrete Concepts Group for the initial installation.

Can I put stencilled or stamped concrete over my existing driveway?

In some cases, a concrete resurfacing overlay can be applied over an existing concrete slab, provided it is in good structural condition. This can be a cost-effective way to get a new decorative finish. We would need to assess the existing concrete slab to determine its suitability.

Which option adds more value to my home?

Both decorative options will add value to your home. However, due to its premium, realistic appearance, a well-executed stamped concrete installation typically offers a higher return on investment by significantly boosting kerb appeal and perceived value.

Ready to Transform Your Space?

Whether you’re leaning towards the intricate patterns of stencilled concrete or the realistic textures of stamped concrete, Concrete Concepts Group is here to bring your vision to life. We pride ourselves on quality workmanship and exceptional customer service across Brisbane. For a no-obligation, free quote on your project, contact our friendly team today. Call 0424 463 268 or get a free quote at concreteconcepts.org.

title: Concrete Crossover Permits in Brisbane: What You Need to Know (2026)
excerpt: Navigating Brisbane's crossover permit process can be complex. This guide details the BCC's application types, costs, and when you need a permit for your driveway.
content:
Concrete Crossover Permits in Brisbane: What You Need to Know

For many Brisbane homeowners, creating the perfect kerb appeal is a significant part of the Australian dream. Every detail, from the manicured lawn to the stylish fence, is carefully curated. Yet, one of the most functionally critical and often underestimated elements of a home's exterior is the driveway crossover. A professionally constructed crossover not only provides a seamless transition from the road to your property but also significantly enhances its value and aesthetic. However, before you can even think about pouring a single metre of concrete, you must navigate the intricate world of council regulations. This comprehensive guide is designed to demystify the process of obtaining a crossover permit Brisbane, covering everything from the initial application to the final construction costs.

What Exactly is a Crossover and Why is Council Approval So Important?

Think of a vehicle crossover as the official welcome mat to your property, starting right at the street. It is the section of your driveway that extends from the road kerb, across the public footpath or nature strip, and meets your property boundary. Because this essential piece of infrastructure is built on council-owned land, obtaining a driveway crossover council approval is a non-negotiable first step. The Brisbane City Council (BCC) enforces these regulations for several crucial reasons that protect both homeowners and the wider community:

  • Ensuring Public Safety: First and foremost, regulations are in place to prevent crossovers from becoming public hazards. An improperly designed crossover could have a dangerously steep gradient, poor visibility for exiting drivers, or create a trip hazard for pedestrians. The council's standards ensure every crossover is safe for all users.
  • Protecting Public Assets: The ground beneath the nature strip is a complex network of essential services, including water mains, gas lines, stormwater drainage, and critical telecommunications cables like the NBN. A botched construction job could lead to costly and disruptive damage to this infrastructure. The permit process ensures that all underground assets are identified and protected.
  • Maintaining a Standard of Quality: The BCC mandates specific construction standards to ensure every crossover in the city is durable, well-drained, and built to last. This consistency prevents premature cracking, subsidence, and other issues that can arise from substandard work, ensuring longevity and value for money.
  • Upholding Legal Compliance: A new driveway permit Brisbane is a legal requirement. Undertaking work without one is a breach of council bylaws and can lead to significant financial penalties and legal complications. Securing a permit ensures your project is fully compliant from day one.

When is a Vehicle Crossing Permit in QLD an Absolute Must?

The rule of thumb in Brisbane is simple and strict: if you are building, modifying, or removing any part of a vehicle crossover, you need a permit. Many homeowners are surprised to learn that even seemingly minor alterations require council approval. The BCC maintains tight control over any work conducted on public land to ensure safety and quality are never compromised.

You Will Definitely Need a Permit If You Are:

  • Constructing a brand-new driveway for a new home build, which is the most common scenario.
  • Adding a second driveway to your property to accommodate more vehicles or create a separate access point.
  • Altering the physical dimensions of your existing crossover, including widening, narrowing, or changing its location.
  • Conducting major structural repairs to fix issues like severe cracking, sinking, or damage from tree roots.
  • Changing the crossover's surface material, for instance, upgrading from old pavers to modern, durable concrete.

When Might You Get Away Without a Permit?

The circumstances where a permit is not required are extremely limited and typically only cover minor, superficial maintenance. For example, pressure washing your driveway to remove dirt and grime or applying a clear sealant to protect the surface would generally not require a permit. However, the line between cosmetic maintenance and structural work can be ambiguous. For this reason, Concrete Concepts Group strongly advises property owners to always consult with the Brisbane City Council before commencing any work. A quick enquiry can provide peace of mind and save you from the potential nightmare of fines and costly orders to remove and redo any unauthorised construction.

The Brisbane City Council Crossover Application Process Explained

The BCC has developed two clear pathways for obtaining a driveway permit: a simplified Self-Assessment for standard projects and a more comprehensive Full Assessment for those with complexities. Identifying the correct pathway for your project is the crucial first step in your application journey.

Pathway 1: The Quick and Easy Self-Assessment Permit

This online process is the fastest and most cost-effective option, designed for straightforward crossover projects that perfectly align with the council's standard criteria. If your proposed design meets all predefined technical standards—covering aspects like width, gradient, and clearance from public infrastructure—you can often secure your permit almost instantly. This pathway is ideal for projects on flat blocks with no unusual site constraints.

Pathway 2: The Detailed Full Assessment Permit

If your project deviates from the standard criteria in any way, you must apply for a full assessment. This involves a thorough review of your plans by council officers. You will be required to submit a detailed site plan, clear photographs of the proposed location, and potentially other supporting documents. This more rigorous process is necessary for properties with site-specific challenges, such as:

  • Steep or complex slopes that require specific engineering solutions.
  • Proximity to street furniture, power poles, large street trees, or stormwater infrastructure.
  • Requests for non-standard crossover widths or unique, architecturally designed shapes.
  • Locations on busy main roads, near intersections, or in areas with high pedestrian traffic.

The council typically processes these applications within 20 working days. As a fully licensed and insured concreting company (QBCC Licence #15299707), Concrete Concepts Group possesses deep expertise in preparing and lodging successful full assessment applications, ensuring every technical detail is meticulously documented to facilitate a smooth approval.

Decoding the Costs: Understanding Permit Fees vs. Total Project Investment

A common point of confusion for homeowners is the difference between the council's administrative permit fees and the total cost of the construction project. The total investment for a new concrete crossover in Brisbane generally falls between $2,000 and $5,000, but this figure can fluctuate based on several factors.

Cost Component Estimated Price Range
BCC Self-Assessment Permit Fee $20.30 (as of early 2026)
BCC Full Assessment Permit Fee $293.40 (as of early 2026)
Concrete Crossover Construction $100 - $250+ per square metre
Excavation and Site Preparation $500 - $2,000+
Traffic Control (if required on busy roads) $500 - $1,500 per day

*Disclaimer: These prices are indicative only and can be influenced by factors such as the chosen concrete finish (e.g., exposed aggregate is more expensive than a standard broom finish), the amount of excavation required, and site accessibility. For an accurate, fixed-price quote tailored to your specific project, use our online estimate tool or contact our friendly team directly.

How Concrete Concepts Group Streamlines Your Project for a Stress-Free Experience

Why entangle yourself in a web of council paperwork and technical specifications when a seasoned expert can manage it all for you? Concrete Concepts Group provides a comprehensive, end-to-end service designed to make your project as seamless as possible. We don't just pour concrete; we orchestrate the entire project from conception to completion. Our all-inclusive service includes:

  • In-Depth Initial Consultation: We visit your property to conduct a thorough assessment, listen to your vision, and provide expert advice on the most suitable materials and designs for your home and budget.
  • Hassle-Free Permit Management: This is where we truly shine. We take complete ownership of the driveway crossover council approval process. Our team prepares and lodges all necessary documentation, liaises directly with council officers, and ensures your application is fully compliant, saving you time and eliminating stress.
  • Masterful Construction: Our highly skilled and experienced team executes all aspects of the build with precision and care, from the initial site preparation to the final, perfect pour, guaranteeing the highest standards of quality workmanship.

We have cultivated a strong reputation across Brisbane, built on a foundation of reliability, transparency, and superior quality. Our expertise extends to a full suite of concreting services, including stunning driveways, inviting patios, robust slabs, and sturdy retaining walls. We encourage you to read our glowing customer testimonials and explore our extensive service areas.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between a crossover and a driveway?

The crossover is the specific portion of the driveway that resides on council land, connecting the road to your property boundary. The driveway is the part on your private property. While the terms are often used interchangeably, the council permit specifically governs the construction of the crossover.

How long is a crossover permit valid for?

A residential driveway permit issued by the Brisbane City Council is valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issue. If the work is not completed within this timeframe, you will be required to submit a new application.

What are the consequences of building a crossover without a permit?

Building without a vehicle crossing permit QLD is a risky and potentially very expensive mistake. The BCC has the authority to issue substantial fines and can serve you with a notice to remove the non-compliant work, forcing you to bear the full cost of demolition and reinstatement of the council verge.

Can I choose any decorative finish for my crossover?

Generally, yes. The council's primary requirements are that the surface is structurally sound and provides adequate slip resistance. Popular decorative choices like exposed aggregate and coloured concrete are typically approved, allowing you to match the crossover to your home's aesthetic.

What is the maximum width for a residential crossover?

The allowable width is not a one-size-fits-all answer. It depends on several factors, including your property's frontage width and the classification of your road. Brisbane City Council's technical standards provide clear formulas that dictate the minimum and maximum widths to ensure safety and proper functionality. We will calculate the compliant width for your property as part of our service.

Do I need a permit to simply repair my existing crossover?

Yes, if the repairs are structural in nature. While minor cosmetic fixes may not require a permit, any work that involves replacing sections of the crossover, even if it's a like-for-like replacement, requires council approval. It is always the safest and most prudent approach to assume a permit is needed and confirm with the council.

Why is it so important to use a licensed contractor?

Using a QBCC-licensed contractor like Concrete Concepts Group is your ultimate protection. It guarantees that the work is performed to the stringent Australian Standards, is fully insured, and comes with a warranty. Hiring an unlicensed operator exposes you to significant financial, legal, and safety risks, and you will have no recourse if the work is defective.

Don't let the prospect of council paperwork deter you from achieving the perfect entrance to your home. Let the dedicated professionals at Concrete Concepts Group handle the red tape, allowing you to focus on the excitement of your property upgrade. For expert advice and a seamless construction experience from a trusted local business, Call 0424 463 268 or get a free quote at concreteconcepts.org today. For more valuable industry insights and tips, be sure to visit our blog.

title: How Much Does a Concrete Patio Cost in Brisbane? (2026 Guide)
excerpt: Learn how much a concrete patio costs in Brisbane with our 2026 guide. We cover costs per m² for plain, coloured, and exposed aggregate finishes, and explore the key factors that influence the final price.
content:
Transform Your Outdoor Living with a Stylish Concrete Patio

For Brisbane homeowners, an outdoor patio is more than just an addition to a house; it’s a quintessential part of the Queensland lifestyle. It’s where you entertain friends on a balmy evening, enjoy a weekend barbecue with family, or simply relax with a book. When it comes to choosing a material for this vital space, concrete stands out for its durability, versatility, and style. But the big question on everyone's mind is: how much does a concrete patio cost in Brisbane? This comprehensive 2026 guide will break down all the costs involved, so you can plan your project with confidence.

Brisbane Concrete Patio Pricing: A 2026 Snapshot

The cost of a concrete patio in Brisbane is not a one-size-fits-all figure. It varies depending on the finish, size, and complexity of the job. However, to give you a clear starting point, we’ve compiled a table of average costs per square metre (m²) for the most popular patio finishes. These prices typically include labour, materials, and basic site preparation for a standard project.

Concrete Finish Average Cost per Square Metre (m²) Best For
Plain Grey Concrete $75 - $95 Budget-conscious projects, utility areas, or a base for tiles.
Coloured Concrete $85 - $105 Adding a touch of personality and matching your home’s colour scheme.
Exposed Aggregate $100 - $150+ Creating a premium, non-slip, and visually textured surface.

Please note: These prices are indicative and can change based on the specific factors of your project. For an accurate, fixed-price quote, it's always best to consult with a professional concreter.

Key Factors That Influence Your Patio Concreting Price

While the per-square-metre rate is a useful guide, several critical factors can influence the final cost of your outdoor patio in Brisbane. Understanding these will help you budget more effectively.

1. Size and Complexity

It’s simple maths: a larger patio requires more materials and labour, increasing the overall cost. However, the cost per square metre can sometimes decrease on very large projects due to economies of scale. The complexity of the design also plays a significant role. A simple square or rectangular slab will be more affordable than a custom shape with curves, multiple levels, or integrated garden beds.

2. Site Access and Preparation

What’s the access to your proposed patio area like? If our team at Concrete Concepts Group can easily get a mini-excavator and concrete truck to the site, preparation costs will be lower. Tight access that requires manual excavation or the use of a concrete pump will add to the labour costs. Furthermore, the existing ground condition is crucial. A sloped block that needs significant excavation and levelling will cost more to prepare than a flat, clear area. Our excavation services are often a necessary first step.

3. The Choice of Finish

As the pricing table shows, the finish is a major cost determinant. While plain grey concrete is the most economical, decorative options like exposed aggregate involve more materials and a multi-stage process, commanding a higher price. Coloured concrete is a great mid-range option to add aesthetic appeal without the cost of high-end finishes.

4. Reinforcement and Thickness

A standard patio slab is typically 100mm thick and includes steel reinforcement mesh (rebar) to provide strength and prevent cracking. This is suitable for foot traffic and outdoor furniture. If you plan to place a heavy structure on the patio, like a spa or an outdoor kitchen, a thicker slab with stronger reinforcement might be necessary, which will increase material costs. This is similar to the requirements for robust concrete slabs designed for sheds or water tanks.

5. Drainage and Council Requirements

In a city with a subtropical climate like Brisbane, proper drainage is non-negotiable. Your patio must be designed to direct rainwater away from your home’s foundations. This may involve installing channel drains or ensuring the slab has the correct fall. Depending on the size and location of your patio, you may also need to get approval from the Brisbane City Council, which can involve costs for plans and applications. A professional concreter will be aware of these local requirements.

Concrete Patios vs. Timber Decking in Brisbane

Many homeowners find themselves choosing between a concrete patio and a timber deck. Here’s a quick comparison to help you decide:

  • Cost: Concrete is significantly more affordable. Timber decking can cost anywhere from $200 to over $400 per square metre, making concrete a more budget-friendly choice for achieving a large entertaining area.
  • Durability: Concrete is the undisputed winner for longevity. It’s resistant to termites, rot, and fire – all genuine concerns in Queensland. A well-laid concrete patio from a reputable company like Concrete Concepts Group will last for decades with minimal upkeep.
  • Maintenance: Timber decks require regular staining, oiling, and sealing to protect them from the harsh Brisbane sun and rain. Concrete patios, on the other hand, are incredibly low-maintenance. An occasional clean and a re-seal every few years is all that’s needed.
  • Aesthetics: While timber offers a classic, natural look, modern concrete finishes provide a huge range of styles. From the sleek, modern appeal of a polished finish to the natural, earthy tones of exposed aggregate, there’s a concrete look to suit any home.

Maximising Your Return on Investment (ROI)

A concrete patio is not just an expense; it’s an investment in your home and lifestyle. A professionally constructed outdoor living area is a highly sought-after feature for homebuyers in Brisbane, significantly increasing your property’s value. It extends your usable living space, creating a seamless flow between indoors and outdoors. By choosing a durable, low-maintenance material like concrete, you ensure this value is added without creating a future burden of costly upkeep. To get an idea of the value you could add, check out our project reviews and see the transformations we’ve completed.

Why Trust a Licensed Professional?

It might be tempting to hire a cheap, unlicensed operator to save a few dollars, but this is a risky gamble. A poor concreting job can lead to cracking, pooling water, and an uneven finish, costing you more in the long run to fix. Always choose a fully licensed and insured professional. Concrete Concepts Group is proud to hold a QBCC Licence (#15299707), giving you peace of mind that your project is in the hands of qualified experts who adhere to the highest industry standards. We don’t just pour concrete; we craft functional and beautiful spaces, from driveways to retaining walls.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does it take to install a concrete patio?

For an average-sized patio (around 25-30m²), the process typically takes 2-4 days. This includes excavation, forming up, pouring the concrete, and the initial finishing. The concrete then needs to cure, which takes several days before you can walk on it and 28 days to reach full strength.

Do I need council approval for a patio in Brisbane?

Generally, if the patio is uncovered and at ground level, you may not need approval. However, rules can vary, especially if the structure is large, close to a boundary, or includes a roof. It's always best to check the latest Brisbane City Council guidelines or consult with your concreter.

Can you pour a new concrete patio over an old one?

It’s generally not recommended. Pouring over an existing, cracked slab can lead to the new slab cracking as well. The best practice is to remove the old slab and prepare a fresh, stable foundation for the new patio.

What is the best concrete finish for a pool surround?

Exposed aggregate is an excellent choice for pool surrounds. Its textured surface provides natural slip resistance, which is a crucial safety feature around wet areas. It also looks fantastic and is comfortable underfoot.

How can I calculate how much concrete I need?

You can use our online concrete calculator to get an estimate. Simply enter the length, width, and thickness of your desired patio to determine the volume of concrete required in cubic metres.

What areas do you service?

Concrete Concepts Group services a wide range of suburbs across Brisbane. You can check our full service area list on our areas page to see if we cover your location.

Ready to Build Your Dream Patio?

Investing in a concrete patio is a smart choice for any Brisbane homeowner. It offers unmatched durability, low maintenance, and a fantastic return on investment. If you’re ready to transform your outdoor space, the team at Concrete Concepts Group is here to help. We specialise in creating high-quality, stylish, and affordable concrete patios tailored to your home and lifestyle. For more ideas, check out our blog.

Call 0424 463 268 or get a free quote at concreteconcepts.org today!
